bull_bear.body: Focus on completing bamboo commissioning and organic capacity ramp; Operating cash flow of INR 86.3cr supports working capital and modest capex; No M&A mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension affecting raw material logistics; Inability to fully pass through 22-25% raw material price hikes (customers accepting only 10-12%); Delay in bamboo commercialization; Customer concentration (IKEA 55%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges short-term headwinds (Q4 disruptions, margin pressure) but emphasizes structural growth, improved gross margins, and strong cash flows as foundations for FY27 recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Recycled polymer volume grew 12.4% YoY to 8,022 MT, signaling sustainability push; 8-week lag in price pass-through for largest customer creates temporary margin gap; 90% of exports are FOB, mitigating freight risk despite port congestion.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Sharp post-IPO deleveraging: debt to equity moved 1.09 (FY23), 0.70 (FY24), 0.88 (FY25) to 0.13 (FY26), with non-current borrowings falling from Rs 101.8 Cr to Rs 55.9 Cr and current borrowings from Rs 116.8 Cr to Rs 24.4 Cr, while shareholders' funds rose from Rs 248.8 Cr to Rs 613.5 Cr (standalone FY26).
- FY26 cash flows show the IPO and the capex cycle together: net cash from financing activities of Rs 175.3 Cr against net cash used in investing activities of Rs 183.5 Cr (standalone), taking cash and cash equivalents to Rs 86.5 Cr standalone / Rs 89.4 Cr consolidated at FY26-end from Rs 8.4 Cr a year earlier.
- Returns were diluted by the equity issue - the deck states ROCE and ROE 'declined majorly due to issue of equity shares during IPO', with ROCE at 17.4%, 22.3%, 17.0% and 10.3% and ROE at 19.7%, 24.9%, 21.0% and 8.3% across FY23-FY26.
- Working capital discipline with net working capital days of 69, 57, 74 and 57 across FY23-FY26; both the bamboo expansion and the NECBDC framework are explicitly described as maintaining capital discipline and full commercial flexibility.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Exports: 83% of revenue (Europe 58%, UK 12%, US 12%); Domestic: 17% (All-Time branded 15%, White label 2%); IKEA contribution: 55% in Q4 (vs 57% prior); Third largest customer grew 225%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility and supply chain disruptions hurting margins temporarily | Supreme Industries | beneficiary | Med | Larger peer with diversified portfolio may gain share if smaller exporters struggle with working capital during price hikes |
| Shift to sustainable alternatives and regulatory push for non-plastic materials | Greenpanel Industries | beneficiary | Low | Bamboo entry by All Time validates the segment but Greenpanel remains the pure-play leader |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Recognized as the largest exporter of plastic houseware and plastic furniture from India (Plexconcil India), with an export footprint across 29 countries including the European Union, the United Kingdom and the United States, and a three-star export house certificate issued by DGFT-MOCI.
- Operates predominantly as a B2B white-label manufacturing partner for global retailers across kitchen, storage, cleaning, bath, organisation and junior categories; the value proposition rests on three stated pillars - design-to-delivery integration, high-volume automated manufacturing, and sticky customer relationships driven by long product lifecycles, repeated SKU refreshes and embedded supply chains.
- The model is claimed to result in repeat orders, long customer tenures and limited price-led competition, particularly in export markets; among the top 20 customers as on FY26, 7 relationships exceed 15 years, 5 are between 10 and 15 years, 7 are between 5 and 10 years and 1 is under 5 years.
- Alongside white-label, the company markets products under the 'All Time' brand in India; the deck's Revenue Break-up shows the export/domestic split moving from 88%/12% in FY23 to 83%/17% in FY26, with domestic scaling described as central to the diversification strategy.
- Industry framing: rising private-label penetration, retailer supplier consolidation and increasing SKU complexity mean growth is 'increasingly captured by manufacturers that operate as strategic supply partners rather than commodity vendors', with India favoured as a China+1 sourcing base.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Input-cost and logistics shock] The West Asia crisis triggered an unprecedented spike in polymer prices from March 2026, while port congestion and container non-availability disrupted both raw material inflows and export shipments; management says raw material prices remain volatile and could see further near-term fluctuation depending on how the geopolitical situation evolves.
- [Trade policy] The EU-India FTA, the evolving US-India trade framework and the China+1 strategy are cited as expected tailwinds for India's sourcing attractiveness; management states the US business 'continues to gain momentum irrespective of tariff considerations', with growing project wins from marquee accounts.
- [Government MoU] ATPL entered an MoU with NECBDC, a statutory body under MDoNER, Government of India, and is empanelled as a Product and Market Development Partner for engineered bamboo initiatives, initially anchored in Assam and Nagaland, covering prototyping of bamboo boards and panels, process and quality standardisation, certification readiness including FSC, and domestic and export market linkage; the framework is explicitly non-exclusive and non-binding, with future commercial engagement to be pursued through separate agreements.
- [Incorporation date contradiction] The Company Snapshot states 'Incorporated in 1971', while the evolution timeline dates the 'Incorporation of our Company' to 2001 and attributes 1971 to setting up the small 'Chhaya Plastics' factory in Mumbai; the CIN shown is L25209MH2001PLC131139.
- [Corporate structure] Wholly owned subsidiaries are All Time Plastics Pte. Ltd. (incorporated 2024) and All Time Bamboo Private Limited (incorporated 2025, for bamboo consumerware); the company was listed on BSE and NSE in 2025 and crossed INR 500 crore in revenue in 2024.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin expanded to 41.9% in Q4 (vs 39.1% YoY) due to product mix; EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% due to higher depreciation (INR 29cr) and employee/contract labor costs; Raw material prices down 10-15% from peaks but only 10-12% pass-through accepted by customers temporarily.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Targeting 70-75% capacity utilization in FY27 (up from 73% weighted avg in FY26); Margin: Expect EBITDA margin recovery to historical levels (18-19%) in H2FY27 as fixed costs absorb; Order inflow: Stable, deferred Q4 volumes (~10-15%) moving to Q1; Capex: INR 15cr for bamboo unit commissioning in H2FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No cancellations reported; ~10-15% of Q4 volumes (approx. INR 3-5cr) deferred to Q1FY27 due to port congestion and raw material delays; Customers rolling out forecasts despite price hikes.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Bamboo board unit (3,000 cubic meters capacity) to start revenue contribution in H2FY27 with potential INR 60cr revenue at full utilization; Domestic B2C target raised to 22-25% mix over next 12-18 months.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Q4FY26 revenue dipped 1.6% YoY due to West Asia-driven supply chain disruptions causing shipment deferrals, while FY26 PAT fell 24.7% due to elevated fixed costs from new capacity; however, gross margins improved sequentially to 41.9% and a strategic pivot to domestic markets (17% mix) plus a new bamboo vertical provides clear recovery levers for FY27.
